job.style: a step-by-step explanation of a process

response.passage: Navigating the internet safely requires understanding how your digital footprint works. First, remember that private browsing or Incognito mode only prevents your local browser history from being saved on your device; it does not hide your activity from your internet service provider or the websites you visit. Second, when creating passwords, avoid simple patterns like replacing letters with numbers, such as 'p@ssw0rd', because these are easily guessed by automated software. Instead, use long, unique phrases for every single account to ensure that a breach in one service does not compromise your entire digital life. Third, never share your OTP with anyone, regardless of who they claim to be. An OTP is a critical security layer, and no legitimate bank representative will ever call you to ask for it. Finally, be aware that deleting a post or setting a profile to private does not guarantee total anonymity. Once content is shared online, it can be screenshotted or saved by others, meaning it is never truly gone from the internet. Always treat online interactions with the same caution you would use in public spaces, as digital actions have real-world consequences.
response.summary: Staying safe online involves using unique passwords, keeping OTPs private, and understanding that digital actions are often permanent. Privacy settings and incognito modes have limitations that users must recognize to protect their data.
